diagnosis: tests/architecture/test_config_in_env.py::test_database_url_env_var_overrides_connection (T10) monkeypatches DATABASE_URL to a bogus DSN and calls importlib.reload(app.database) to verify resolved_url() picks it up. app.database's engine/SessionLocal are module-level singletons, and get_db() reads the module-global SessionLocal at call time (not a captured value), so the reload rebinds the SAME connection every other module's already-imported get_db reference uses. The test's own finally-block then calls monkeypatch.delenv('DATABASE_URL', raising=False) (deleting the var outright, not restoring whatever value was present before this test ran) and reloads app.database again to 'restore' it. Since the real verify environment already had an explicit DATABASE_URL set (the ephemeral-verify DSN app/database.py's own docstring describes), deleting it makes the restore-reload fall through to the Lakebase-metadata/local-fallback branch of make_engine() instead of reconstructing the original explicit-DSN engine, permanently rebinding the shared engine/SessionLocal to a DIFFERENT connection target for the rest of the process. conftest.py's db_session fixture captured the ORIGINAL SessionLocal at collection time (before any reload) so it keeps querying the correct branch DB, while every request made through the API's get_db() dependency after this fitness test runs now writes through the rebound (wrong/fallback) connection. That is exactly why only the two tests that write via the API and then re-verify persistence through db_session fail: test_filing_a_valid_stock_record_for_a_fresh_pair_persists_it_and_confirms (T1, checks 'a stock record exists in the database' via db_session after a client.post) and test_refiling_the_same_pair_with_a_different_quantity_resolves_to_a_single_row (T7, checks 'exactly one stock record exists' via db_session after two client.post calls) both find zero matching rows because the row landed on the rebound connection, not the one db_session reads from. Tests that only assert the immediate HTTP response body (T9), or read back through the same client connection within one test (T2), or need no persistence at all (T5), are unaffected, and pytest-order confirms test_config_in_env.py collects and runs before tests/step_defs/test_S1_file_stock_record.py in this suite. This is an order-dependent test-pollution regression in the T10 fitness test's own restore logic, not an intentional behavior change from AC1-record-filed-and-confirmed.
fixDirective: In tests/architecture/test_config_in_env.py::test_database_url_env_var_overrides_connection, capture the ORIGINAL DATABASE_URL value (os.environ.get('DATABASE_URL')) before calling monkeypatch.setenv with the bogus DSN. In the finally block, restore that captured original value with monkeypatch.setenv(...) when it was present (falling back to monkeypatch.delenv('DATABASE_URL', raising=False) only when it was originally unset), then importlib.reload(database), so the module-level engine/SessionLocal singleton is rebuilt against the SAME connection target it had before the test ran instead of falling through to a different make_engine() branch.
